# FAQ-012 Engineering FAQ #12
Revision: Rev A

Q: What should I do when the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) trips?
A: Background: The dust collector pressure differential is an indicator of media loading or airflow restriction. The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 2025 Pa. Rationale: This alarm value is the confirmed threshold for initiating filter inspection and cleaning to prevent loss of blast quality and motor overload. Actions:
- Stop material flow to the cabinet and place the cell in a safe condition.
- Visually inspect the collector housing and filter access panels for signs of damage or bypass.
- Perform filter cleaning per the maintenance checklist in SB-1033.
- If cleaning restores acceptable airflow, document the event and restart operations.
Records to keep: filter inspection checklist, filter cleaning log, and the alarm event entry in the maintenance log. Reference: see SB-1033 and QS-PROC-08 for procedural and quality disposition requirements.

Q: What is the acceptable target for billet temperature before charging into Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03)?
A: Background: Proper billet temperature is critical for forging grain structure and die life. The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 1180 °C. Rationale: Operators must confirm billets reach this target prior to transfer to the forge to ensure material plasticity and reduce risk of internal defects. Actions:
- Verify process temperature readouts against target prior to transfer.
- If readout is below target, hold the billet in the heater and follow heat-up practices in SOP-P3-L3-02 until target is achieved.
- If readout is above target, follow cooling and qualification steps in QS-PROC-08 before forging.
Records to keep: temperature logs, operator shift handover notes, and any nonconformance reports per QS-PROC-08. Reference: SOP-P3-L3-02 for heater operation and QS-PROC-08 for disposition.

Q: How frequently should way lube be refilled on Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02)?
A: Background: Way lubrication prevents wear and maintains machining accuracy and surface finish. The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours. Rationale: This interval reflects combined factors of machine duty cycle and lubricant drain characteristics; adherence reduces risk of accelerated wear and guideway scoring. Actions:
- Schedule refills to align with routine machine checks and documented preventive maintenance.
- During refill, inspect reservoirs and feed lines for contamination and verify lubricant grade.
- Log refill actions including machine ID, lubricant lot, and operator initials.
Records to keep: way lube refill log entry and machine preventive maintenance record. Reference: SOP-P3-L3-02 for lubricant handling and QS-PROC-08 for quality records.

Q: What setpoint should be used for the austenitizing stage in Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02)?
A: Background: Austenitizing temperature determines phase transformation necessary for subsequent cooling and mechanical properties. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 855 °C. Rationale: Use of this setpoint ensures the material attains the required austenitic structure without excessive grain growth. Actions:
- Program the furnace control to the specified setpoint and verify with independent temperature monitoring prior to start.
- Hold time and cooling profiles remain per the applicable heat treat procedure; deviations require approval and record in QS-PROC-08.
Records to keep: heat treatment cycle log, controlled atmosphere records if applicable, and post-heat-treat hardness or metallurgical test results. Reference: QS-PROC-08 for approval and SB-1033 for furnace safety checks.

Q: What is the minimum acceptable coil cooling water flow for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03)?
A: Background: Cooling water flow is critical to protect induction coil integrity and prevent overheating failures. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Rationale: Maintaining at least this flow prevents thermal damage and supports expected heater lifetime. Actions:
- Verify flow rate with the in-line flow indicator prior to and during operation.
- If flow drops below the minimum, halt induction current immediately and follow troubleshooting steps in SB-1033.
- Inspect inlet strainers, valves, and pump performance; restore flow and perform system test before returning to production.
Records to keep: flow check log, pump maintenance records, and any incident reports filed under QS-PROC-08. Reference: SB-1033 for emergency stop criteria and QS-PROC-08 for recordkeeping.

Related documents: QS-PROC-08, SB-1033, SOP-P3-L3-02
